CLINICAL CONTEXT & STYLE NOTE
This document is written in the style commonly utilised by GPs, Occupational Health physicians, and consultant
psychiatrists. It concentrates on objective clinical information and functional impact, rather than legal issues. 
2. MEDICAL BACKGROUND
Long-Term Mental Health Condition
I have experienced a long-term psychiatric illness since 2001, which has had a significant impact on my ability to
work over many years.
My condition has been recognised by both my employer and the Group Income Protection insurer throughout my
period of absence.
Following a relapse during 2005, I remained employed by CACI Ltd but was unable to return successfully to work
despite attempts at vocational rehabilitation.
Although I have remained absent from work for an extended period, my health has not remained static. There have

If you are off sick, we may want to refer you to Occupational Health to get more information about your

information we have received. 
Once your appointment is booked, it is important you attend. If you need to cancel or reschedule, you

incurred.  Appointments are done by video conference, there is no requirement to travel.  
Disability-related absence

citations: Sickness Absence Policy.pdf, p.9
source_assertions.text:
Source assertion: If you are off sick due to a disability-related illness, your manager will try to support you to return to work. 
They might refer you to Occupational Health to find out more about your condition, how it may affect you 
at work and whether there are any adjustments we could make to help. 
These absences might count towards the absence triggers in some circumstances. However, it might be a 
reasonable adjustment to agree a revised absence trigger with you for absences related to a disability or 
to not include them when calculating absences triggers. If you have any questions or concerns about 
disability-related absence, speak to your manager. Managers should contact HR for advice on revising 
absence triggers for employees with disabilities. 
Alternative employment 
If you are unable to return to your own job, your Line Manager and HR will consider suitable alternative 
employment, although we will not be obliged to create new positions for this purpose.

time away is below 1 hour. Where time away from work to attend such appointments exceeds 1 hour, you 
should agree with your manager how best to make up any lost time.

regular medical appointments or receive treatment, these appointments will be accommodated where 
possible. There are additional considerations where the health condition may be classed as a disability

Purpose and Principles 
This procedure should be read alongside the Company's Sickness Absence Policy and applies 
where an employee is unable to fulfil the requirements of their role due to ill health and dismissal 
on the grounds of capability is being considered. 
The Company will consider all relevant medical evidence, including Occupational Health advice, 
and whether any reasonable adjustments or suitable alternative employment would enable the 
employee to return to work. 
Where, following consultation and a review of the available evidence, the Company concludes 
that the employee is unable to perform the essential requirements of their role, with or without 
reasonable adjustments, and no suitable alternative employment is available, employment may 
be terminated on the grounds of capability, following the required statutory process. 
Where an employee who has been issued with notice of termination subsequently states that they

Source assertion: be terminated on the grounds of capability, following the required statutory process. 
Where an employee who has been issued with notice of termination subsequently states that they 
are fit to return to work, the Company will not be required to withdraw that notice solely based 
on that assertion or evidence of an improvement in their condition. Any decision to withdraw 
notice will be based on a full assessment of the employee's ability to undertake the essential 
duties of their role on a sustained basis, considering up-to-date medical evidence, Occupational 
Health advice, the effectiveness of  any proposed adjustments, business requirements and the 
availability of a suitable role. 
Where the evidence does not support a sustainable return to work, or no reasonable adjustments 
would enable the employee to fulfil the requirements of the role, the dismissal on the grounds of 
capability may proceed.

disabled under the Equality Act 2010, you are expected to assist the Company to the extent you are able

Source assertion: disabled under the Equality Act 2010, you are expected to assist the Company to the extent you are able 
in establishing the adjustments that might be required. 
Occupational health  
If you are off sick, we may want to refer you to Occupational Health to get more information about your 
condition. You do not have to agree, but if you do not, we will manage your absence based on the limited 
information we have received. 
Once your appointment is booked, it is important you attend. If you need to cancel or reschedule, you 
must contact HR immediately giving a minimum of 72 hours’ notice or a cancellation charge will be 
incurred.  Appointments are done by video conference, there is no requirement to travel.  
Disability-related absence 
If you think you have a disability, talk to your manager about it and discuss any adjustments you need.  
If you are off sick due to a disability-related illness, your manager will try to support you to return to work.

citations: Sickness Absence Policy.pdf, p.9
source_assertions.text:
Source assertion: If you are off sick due to a disability-related illness, your manager will try to support you to return to work. 
They might refer you to Occupational Health to find out more about your condition, how it may affect you 
at work and whether there are any adjustments we could make to help. 
These absences might count towards the absence triggers in some circumstances. However, it might be a 
reasonable adjustment to agree a revised absence trigger with you for absences related to a disability or 
to not include them when calculating absences triggers. If you have any questions or concerns about 
disability-related absence, speak to your manager. Managers should contact HR for advice on revising 
absence triggers for employees with disabilities. 
Alternative employment 
If you are unable to return to your own job, your Line Manager and HR will consider suitable alternative 
employment, although we will not be obliged to create new positions for this purpose.

citations: Sickness Absence Policy.pdf, p.9
source_assertions.text:
Source assertion: If you are unable to return to your own job, your Line Manager and HR will consider suitable alternative 
employment, although we will not be obliged to create new positions for this purpose.  
If you are to return to work in an alternative role, revised terms and conditions will be agreed with you 
before such return. 
Incapacity 
Where you are not capable of returning to your old job due to ill-health, even if reasonable adjustments 
are made, and no suitable alternative employment can be found, notice of termination may be issued 
following a period of consultation.  Such termination will usually be on the grounds of capability.  In such 
circumstances pay may be given in lieu of notice. 
If during the currency of any notice of termination given to you pursuant to this policy, you provide 
satisfactory medical evidence to the effect that you have fully recovered from any physical and/or mental

citations: Sickness Absence Policy.pdf, p.10
source_assertions.text:
Source assertion: Sickness Absence Policy / © 20266 CACI Confidential     10 
health problems and that no recurrence of illness or incapacity can reasonably be anticipated, you agree 
that we may withdraw the notice unless, by that date, a replacement for you has been appointed.  
Where you are pregnant, you will be managed considerately and in accordance with employment and 
health and safety legislation and the Company’s maternity policy. Pregnancy related absences during the 
pregnancy and maternity leave and time off for antenatal appointments will not be considered when 
reviewing an individual’s attendance record.  In addition, maternity, paternity, adoption, and parental 
leave will not be classed as absence for the purpose of attendance monitoring.  
Time off for medical appointments 
Reasonable requests to attend medical appointments will be granted and accommodated where 
possible. Employees should make every effort to organise attendance at such appointments outside of

citations: Sickness Absence Policy.pdf, p.10
source_assertions.text:
Source assertion: review procedure and, where appropriate, our disciplinary procedure. 
Lateness which is not associated with short term frequent absences will be investigated and managed 
through our disciplinary or capability procedure as appropriate. 
Unauthorised absence 
Unauthorised absence, for example leaving the Company’s premises without permission or failing to 
comply with our notification and certification procedures are usually regarded as disciplinary matters and 
will be dealt with under our disciplinary procedure. 
Further support 
If you have any questions about how you need to report your absence or about the Company’s approach 
to managing absence, please speak to your manager. If managers need advice, they should contact HR.  
We have an Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) who can provide employees with support. You can 
contact the EAP on 0800 023 2269.

source_assertions.text:
Source assertion: be terminated on the grounds of capability, following the required statutory process. 
Where an employee who has been issued with notice of termination subsequently states that they 
are fit to return to work, the Company will not be required to withdraw that notice solely based 
on that assertion or evidence of an improvement in their condition. Any decision to withdraw 
notice will be based on a full assessment of the employee's ability to undertake the essential 
duties of their role on a sustained basis, considering up-to-date medical evidence, Occupational 
Health advice, the effectiveness of  any proposed adjustments, business requirements and the 
availability of a suitable role. 
Where the evidence does not support a sustainable return to work, or no reasonable adjustments 
would enable the employee to fulfil the requirements of the role, the dismissal on the grounds of 
capability may proceed.

Right of Appeal 
An employee who is dismissed on the grounds of capability may appeal the decision in writing 
within five working days of receiving the outcome letter, stating the grounds of appeal. An appeal 
meeting will be arranged and heard by a manager not previously i nvolved in the case where 
possible. The outcome of the appeal will be final. 
 
Special Considerations 
Pregnancy-related sickness absence, maternity leave, paternity leave, adoption leave, parental 
leave and time off for antenatal appointments will be managed in line with relevant legislation 
and Company policies and will not be considered when assessing attendance or capability under 
this procedure. 
 
The Company reserves the right to change this document at any time to reflect statutory 
changes or changes in Company Policy or process.

source_assertions.text:
Source assertion: C&W WorkWell Referral Form
WorkWell is a programme funded by DWP and part of the UK Government’s measures to better
join up health and employment support . It aims to align the work and health landscape at local
level to support retention or return to employment for individuals with mental health or health-
related barriers. WorkWell can support an individual by providing:
Low intensity support for individuals either in work and struggling to retain or return to
their employment due to their mental health or a health-related work barrier
                                                                         or
Low intensity support for individuals recently unemployed and facing a barrier to return to
work due to mental health or a health-related work barrier.
WorkWell will provide support from a Journey Guide to explore support options and create a
tailored plan to retain or return to work.

Purpose and Principles 
This procedure should be read alongside the Company's Sickness Absence Policy and applies 
where an employee is unable to fulfil the requirements of their role due to ill health and dismissal 
on the grounds of capability is being considered. 
The Company will consider all relevant medical evidence, including Occupational Health advice, 
and whether any reasonable adjustments or suitable alternative employment would enable the 
employee to return to work. 
Where, following consultation and a review of the available evidence, the Company concludes 
that the employee is unable to perform the essential requirements of their role, with or without 
reasonable adjustments, and no suitable alternative employment is available, employment may 
be terminated on the grounds of capability, following the required statutory process. 
Where an employee who has been issued with notice of termination subsequently states that they

Source assertion: be terminated on the grounds of capability, following the required statutory process. 
Where an employee who has been issued with notice of termination subsequently states that they 
are fit to return to work, the Company will not be required to withdraw that notice solely based 
on that assertion or evidence of an improvement in their condition. Any decision to withdraw 
notice will be based on a full assessment of the employee's ability to undertake the essential 
duties of their role on a sustained basis, considering up-to-date medical evidence, Occupational 
Health advice, the effectiveness of  any proposed adjustments, business requirements and the 
availability of a suitable role. 
Where the evidence does not support a sustainable return to work, or no reasonable adjustments 
would enable the employee to fulfil the requirements of the role, the dismissal on the grounds of 
capability may proceed.

Current Capability 
You asked whether I consider myself fit to return to work. 
I do not consider it possible, on the information presently available, to express any reliable 
opinion regarding my current capability for work until an up-to-date Occupational Health 
assessment has been completed, relevant medical evidence has been obtained and any 
recommended reasonable adjustments have been identified and properly evaluated. 
While historical medical evidence accurately reflected my condition when prepared, my 
health has improved in key respects. Any assessment of my capability should be based 
upon my current medical condition and functional capacity, rather than solely upon 
historical medical evidence, and should take into account any reasonable adjustments that 
may enable me to return to work safely and sustainably.

source_assertions.text:
Source assertion: Changes in Medical Circumstances 
When I completed the Claims Services International Declaration of Long-Term Incapacity 
in November 2025, my responses accurately reflected my circumstances at that time and 
were provided solely to assess entitlement under the Group Income Protection Scheme. 
Since then, my health has improved. In addition to ongoing treatment for my long-term 
mental health condition, I have been prescribed Wegovy (semaglutide) under medical 
supervision as part of a structured weight management programme. Together with lifestyle 
changes, this has enabled me to lose substantial weight, improve physical fitness, and 
enhance my overall wellbeing, which has positively impacted my mental health. 
While I continue to experience longstanding symptoms associated with Borderline 
Personality Disorder, anxiety, and depression—and am not suggesting I am currently fully 
fit to return—my health has improved noticeably since November 2025.

Source assertion: Relevance to the Claim
1. Confirms that CACI were planning the Claimant’s return to work, and that Jeet Khaira 
and Nigel Phillips had direct managerial involvement.
2. The statement “if all goes well” by HR on behalf of Jeet Khaira shows the anticipated 
outcome of the meeting – a critical precursor to the subsequent demotion and pay cut.
3. Demonstrates CACI’s awareness of the need for reasonable adjustments and structured 
rehabilitation, as advised by UnumProvident, yet these steps were never implemented.
4. Corroborates that the Claimant was fit, willing and proactive in returning to work, refuting 
any assertion that he was disengaged or unfit.
5. Supports claims under:
• s.15 Equality Act 2010 – Discrimination arising from disability (adverse treatment 
following disability-related absence);
• s.20 EqA 2010 – Failure to make reasonable adjustments; and
• s.98 Employment Rights Act 1996 – Unfair dismissal (procedural and substantive).

Source assertion: Appendix L5 – Leadership Continuity (Weir 
and Khaira)
Claimant: Mr Arshad Shafi
Respondent: CACI Limited
Bundle Section: Part 10 – Appendices
Date prepared: October 2025
Summary
This appendix records the continuity of corporate leadership within CACI Limited relevant to the 
Claimant’s employment and subsequent dispute.
It confirms that Ms Tracy Weir (President & Chief Executive since November 2024, with 
approximately 26 years’ service) and Mr Jeet Khaira (former Managing Director, Information & 
Management Systems Division, departed 2024) both held senior executive roles during and after the
period 2000 – 2005 that forms the basis of the Claimant’s case.
Their overlapping tenures demonstrate that CACI Ltd retains long-standing institutional knowledge 
of the events underlying this claim and continued access to relevant HR, occupational-health and 
insurer (Unum) records.

Occupational health  
If you are off sick, we may want to refer you to Occupational Health to get more information about your 
condition. You do not have to agree, but if you do not, we will manage your absence based on the limited 
information we have received. 
Once your appointment is booked, it is important you attend. If you need to cancel or reschedule, you 
must contact HR immediately giving a minimum of 72 hours’ notice or a cancellation charge will be 
incurred.  Appointments are done by video conference, there is no requirement to travel.  
Disability-related absence 
If you think you have a disability, talk to your manager about it and discuss any adjustments you need.  
If you are off sick due to a disability-related illness, your manager will try to support you to return to work.

Source assertion: If you are off sick due to a disability-related illness, your manager will try to support you to return to work. 
They might refer you to Occupational Health to find out more about your condition, how it may affect you 
at work and whether there are any adjustments we could make to help. 
These absences might count towards the absence triggers in some circumstances. However, it might be a 
reasonable adjustment to agree a revised absence trigger with you for absences related to a disability or 
to not include them when calculating absences triggers. If you have any questions or concerns about 
disability-related absence, speak to your manager. Managers should contact HR for advice on revising 
absence triggers for employees with disabilities. 
Alternative employment 
If you are unable to return to your own job, your Line Manager and HR will consider suitable alternative 
employment, although we will not be obliged to create new positions for this purpose.

join up health and employment support . It aims to align the work and health landscape at local
level to support retention or return to employment for individuals with mental health or health-
related barriers. WorkWell can support an individual by providing:
Low intensity support for individuals either in work and struggling to retain or return to
their employment due to their mental health or a health-related work barrier
                                                                         or
Low intensity support for individuals recently unemployed and facing a barrier to return to
work due to mental health or a health-related work barrier.
WorkWell will provide support from a Journey Guide to explore support options and create a
tailored plan to retain or return to work.

This procedure should be read alongside the Company's Sickness Absence Policy and applies

An employee who is absent from work due to sickness must follow the procedure for every period of 
unplanned absence outlined in this policy. If the procedure is not followed, this may be viewed as 
unauthorised absence which could lead to a formal disciplin ary process and may impact your pay.

If an employee is unwell during a period of annual leave, they should inform their manager of this on the 
first day of their sickness and provide a fit note which covers the full period of their absence. They will be 
considered unwell from the date outlined on the fit note. Where this process has been followed, they will 
be entitled to take the annual leave that fell within their period of ill health later.  
Return to work  
Where you wish to return to work prior to the date noted on a medical certificate / fit note you must 
obtain a signing off note from a healthcare professional prior to attending work.  Where your healthcare 
professional advises that you are not fit to return, you will not be permitted to return to work unless the 
Company has or obtains evidence that it may, at its discretion, rely on in preference to the healthcare

practitioner’s opinion. In any event, the Company reserves the right to suspend you on full p ay on medical 
grounds if it has any concerns about your health, irrespective of any received medical note or opinion.  
To manage sickness absence effectively and consistently we will seek to support staff during periods of 
illness and use the following interventions and procedures to facilitate a return to work, retain staff in 
employment and improve attendance. 
• Return to work discussions and interviews. 
• Keeping in touch during absence. 
• Monitoring and recording absence. 
• Carrying out sickness review meetings. 
• Providing management support. 
• Seeking medical reports and occupational health advice. 
 
Managing absence through these procedures or through the disciplinary process where appropriate.

• Seeking medical reports and occupational health advice. 
 
Managing absence through these procedures or through the disciplinary process where appropriate.  
Where your Line Manager and/or HR have serious concerns about the level or pattern of absences the 
Company may, following a return-to-work interview or during continuing absence, deal with it under the 
disciplinary procedure.  The disciplinary procedure will not, however, normally be used in cases of long-
term sickness absence, and a capability procedure may be invoked.  
Long term sickness  
While the Company is keen to assist employees who are absent, it cannot offer indefinite support. The 
Company will be eager to get any employees on long-term sickness absence back into the workplace as 
effectively as possible, but the employment may need to be terminated if this cannot be achieved. Once

the employee has exhausted their 28-week entitlement to statutory sick pay, or before, the employee’s 
manager or someone from the HR department will discuss with the employee their likely return to work 
date and what work duties they may be able to fulfil.  
The Company will usually require employees who have been absent for one month or more or are 
expected to be absent for one month or more, to return some or all their equipment. This may be 
requested so that the equipment can be redeployed to other employees. Equipment will be returned to 
affected employees immediately upon their return to work.   
If there are regular or persistent absences due to illness, injury etc, the Company is unlikely to be able to 
support this indefinitely, after making reasonable adjustments. Ultimately, employment may be

decision to dismiss. Any appeal should be made in writing to the Head of HR within five working days. The 
employee has the right to be accompanied to the appeal hearing. 
The employee is encouraged to re-apply to join the organisation once the employee is fit to return to 
work. If there is a suitable vacancy, the employee’s application will be given sympathetic consideration.  
Reasonable adjustments 
The Company will comply with its obligations regarding the duty to make reasonable adjustments under 
the Equality Act 2010. Such adjustments may include a reduction in hours, the transfer of certain duties to 
other employees, physical adjustments, and retraining.  Such adjustments may be adopted on a 
temporary or permanent basis depending on the circumstances of each case. If you are, or may be 
disabled under the Equality Act 2010, you are expected to assist the Company to the extent you are able

in establishing the adjustments that might be required. 
Occupational health  
If you are off sick, we may want to refer you to Occupational Health to get more information about your 
condition. You do not have to agree, but if you do not, we will manage your absence based on the limited 
information we have received. 
Once your appointment is booked, it is important you attend. If you need to cancel or reschedule, you 
must contact HR immediately giving a minimum of 72 hours’ notice or a cancellation charge will be 
incurred.  Appointments are done by video conference, there is no requirement to travel.  
Disability-related absence 
If you think you have a disability, talk to your manager about it and discuss any adjustments you need.  
If you are off sick due to a disability-related illness, your manager will try to support you to return to work.

citations: Sickness Absence Policy.pdf, p.9
source_assertions.text:
Source assertion: If you are off sick due to a disability-related illness, your manager will try to support you to return to work. 
They might refer you to Occupational Health to find out more about your condition, how it may affect you 
at work and whether there are any adjustments we could make to help. 
These absences might count towards the absence triggers in some circumstances. However, it might be a 
reasonable adjustment to agree a revised absence trigger with you for absences related to a disability or 
to not include them when calculating absences triggers. If you have any questions or concerns about 
disability-related absence, speak to your manager. Managers should contact HR for advice on revising 
absence triggers for employees with disabilities. 
Alternative employment 
If you are unable to return to your own job, your Line Manager and HR will consider suitable alternative 
employment, although we will not be obliged to create new positions for this purpose.

If you are to return to work in an alternative role, revised terms and conditions will be agreed with you 
before such return. 
Incapacity 
Where you are not capable of returning to your old job due to ill-health, even if reasonable adjustments 
are made, and no suitable alternative employment can be found, notice of termination may be issued 
following a period of consultation.  Such termination will usually be on the grounds of capability.  In such 
circumstances pay may be given in lieu of notice. 
If during the currency of any notice of termination given to you pursuant to this policy, you provide 
satisfactory medical evidence to the effect that you have fully recovered from any physical and/or mental

health problems and that no recurrence of illness or incapacity can reasonably be anticipated, you agree 
that we may withdraw the notice unless, by that date, a replacement for you has been appointed.  
Where you are pregnant, you will be managed considerately and in accordance with employment and 
health and safety legislation and the Company’s maternity policy. Pregnancy related absences during the 
pregnancy and maternity leave and time off for antenatal appointments will not be considered when 
reviewing an individual’s attendance record.  In addition, maternity, paternity, adoption, and parental 
leave will not be classed as absence for the purpose of attendance monitoring.

Background
1. My name is Arshad Shafi. I was employed by CACI Limited as a Senior Principal 
Consultant from October 2000. I am a British Pakistani Muslim man.
2. In 2001, I suffered a psychiatric breakdown following sustained racial and religious 
harassment while on assignment in Liverpool. Following this, I was placed on long-term 
sick leave, receiving two-thirds of my salary through the Respondent’s insurer, Unum.
3. In 2005, I attempted a phased return to work under medical supervision.
Events in 2005
4. At the start of my return, I had a meeting with Mr Jeet (Manjeet) Khaira, my Managing 
Director, and Miguel [surname if known]. In that meeting, I was informed that I would be 
assigned to Newcastle City Council in a Business Analyst role. I understood this to be a 
Principal Consultant-grade assignment. No mention was made of any demotion, and I was 
reassured and happy to be returning to proper work.

Source assertion: If you are off sick due to a disability-related illness, your manager will try to support you to return to work. 
They might refer you to Occupational Health to find out more about your condition, how it may affect you

These absences might count towards the absence triggers in some circumstances. However, it might be a 
reasonable adjustment to agree a revised absence trigger with you for absences related to a disability or 
to not include them when calculating absences triggers. If you have any questions or concerns about 
disability-related absence, speak to your manager. Managers should contact HR for advice on revising 
absence triggers for employees with disabilities. 
Alternative employment 
If you are unable to return to your own job, your Line Manager and HR will consider suitable alternative 
employment, although we will not be obliged to create new positions for this purpose.

source_assertions.text:
Source assertion: resilience.
Busy Working Environments
Busy offices, frequent interruptions, excessive background noise and constantly changing priorities are particularly
difficult for me. I function considerably better in environments that are:
quiet;
structured;
predictable; and
allow uninterrupted periods of concentration.
Travelling and Commuting
One of my most significant remaining difficulties relates to prolonged travelling. Lengthy commuting creates:
increased anxiety;
fatigue;
reduced concentration;
increased stress levels.
For this reason, I believe that home working or predominantly home-based hybrid working would significantly
reduce the impact of my condition.
Fatigue
Although my physical stamina has improved considerably, prolonged periods of psychological pressure continue to
produce mental fatigue. This differs from physical tiredness. Once mentally fatigued, I find it increasingly difficult to
maintain concentration and to process large amounts of information effectively.

source_assertions.text:
Source assertion: Current Overall Position
Overall, I believe my condition has improved compared with previous years. However, I do not consider that I have
returned to my previous level of resilience before my illness. I therefore believe that any return to work would need
to  take  account  of  my  remaining  functional  limitations  and  should  be  supported  by  appropriate  workplace
adjustments where these are considered reasonable and medically appropriate.
Clinical Summary
In summary:
My physical health has improved substantially.
My cardiovascular health has improved.
My weight has reduced to a healthy level.
I exercise regularly.
My mental health symptoms persist but are more stable than previously.
My greatest remaining difficulties relate to anxiety, stress tolerance, prolonged commuting and highly stimulating
work environments.
I remain motivated to explore a safe and sustainable return to suitable employment if this is supported by
appropriate medical advice and workplace adjustments.

Source assertion: Appendix L5 – Leadership Continuity (Weir 
and Khaira)
Claimant: Mr Arshad Shafi
Respondent: CACI Limited
Bundle Section: Part 10 – Appendices
Date prepared: October 2025
Summary
This appendix records the continuity of corporate leadership within CACI Limited relevant to the 
Claimant’s employment and subsequent dispute.
It confirms that Ms Tracy Weir (President & Chief Executive since November 2024, with 
approximately 26 years’ service) and Mr Jeet Khaira (former Managing Director, Information & 
Management Systems Division, departed 2024) both held senior executive roles during and after the
period 2000 – 2005 that forms the basis of the Claimant’s case.
Their overlapping tenures demonstrate that CACI Ltd retains long-standing institutional knowledge 
of the events underlying this claim and continued access to relevant HR, occupational-health and 
insurer (Unum) records.
Relevance to Proceedings

Source assertion: Given the length of time Ash has been absent, a graduated return to work is 
recommended to enable him to rebuild stamina.
I propose the following plan for your consideration:
Week 1 (w/c 16 May): Thurs & Fri – half days
Week 2 (w/c 23 May): Mon, Wed, Fri – half days
Week 3 (w/c 30 May): not working
Week 4 (w/c 6 June): 3 consecutive half days
Week 5 (w/c 13 June): 5 half days
Week 6 (w/c 20 June): 3 full days (Mon, Wed, Fri) and 2 half days
Week 7 (w/c 27 June): 5 full days
Duties should be increased gradually in line with hours.
Weekly 1:1s are recommended to monitor progress and address any issues.
Nigel – please provide a weekly update via email on Ash’s progress.
I understand that Ash will be reporting to Terry Williamson on Thursday and Friday.
If you agree to the plan, it may be beneficial to ensure Terry is aware of how the RTW 
will be structured.
Kind Regards,
Emma Shakespeare, UnumProvident Rehabilitation Consultant”

source_assertions.text:

Purpose and Principles 
This procedure should be read alongside the Company's Sickness Absence Policy and applies 
where an employee is unable to fulfil the requirements of their role due to ill health and dismissal 
on the grounds of capability is being considered. 
The Company will consider all relevant medical evidence, including Occupational Health advice, 
and whether any reasonable adjustments or suitable alternative employment would enable the 
employee to return to work. 
Where, following consultation and a review of the available evidence, the Company concludes 
that the employee is unable to perform the essential requirements of their role, with or without 
reasonable adjustments, and no suitable alternative employment is available, employment may 
be terminated on the grounds of capability, following the required statutory process. 
Where an employee who has been issued with notice of termination subsequently states that they

citations: Procedure_Managing Incapacity related to Capability.pdf, p.2
source_assertions.text:
Source assertion: be terminated on the grounds of capability, following the required statutory process. 
Where an employee who has been issued with notice of termination subsequently states that they 
are fit to return to work, the Company will not be required to withdraw that notice solely based 
on that assertion or evidence of an improvement in their condition. Any decision to withdraw 
notice will be based on a full assessment of the employee's ability to undertake the essential 
duties of their role on a sustained basis, considering up-to-date medical evidence, Occupational 
Health advice, the effectiveness of  any proposed adjustments, business requirements and the 
availability of a suitable role. 
Where the evidence does not support a sustainable return to work, or no reasonable adjustments 
would enable the employee to fulfil the requirements of the role, the dismissal on the grounds of 
capability may proceed.

General principles 
The Company aims to encourage all its employees to maximise their attendance at work whilst recognising 
that employees will, from time to time, be unable to come to work due to sickness.  
Whilst the Company understands that there will inevitably be some absence amongst employees, it must 
also pay due regard to its business needs. If an employee is frequently and persistently absent from work, 
this can damage efficiency and productivity, and  place an additional burden of work on the employee's 
colleagues.  
We will provide a healthy employment environment which promotes the wellbeing of all employees and 
reduces levels of absence, thereby ensuring effective service planning and delivery. We recognise the hard 
work of our employees and will assist those who have been absent to return to work as quickly and fully as

• to provide advice and guidance to managers and employees, 
• to liaise with occupational health (OH) advisors as appropriate, 
• to provide reports and statistics as required. 
Manager responsibilities 
• to understand and observe their responsibilities detailed in the policy, 
• to ensure that all employees are treated with respect and receive fair and consistent treatment, 
• to ensure employees feel valued during periods of sickness absence and in the way their return to work is 
managed, 
• to ensure good health and safety standards in their area and to comply with CACI’s health and safety policies, as 
appropriate, 
• to ensure employees are aware and observe their responsibilities regarding sickness notification and reporting 
procedures,

appropriate action to enable the employee to return to work (eg. stress risk assessment, temporary flexible 
working arrangements),

Notification and recording of absence 
An employee who is absent from work due to sickness must follow the procedure for every period of

If an employee is unwell during a period of annual leave, they should inform their manager of this on the 
first day of their sickness and provide a fit note which covers the full period of their absence. They will be 
considered unwell from the date outlined on the fit note. Where this process has been followed, they will 
be entitled to take the annual leave that fell within their period of ill health later.  
Return to work  
Where you wish to return to work prior to the date noted on a medical certificate / fit note you must 
obtain a signing off note from a healthcare professional prior to attending work.  Where your healthcare 
professional advises that you are not fit to return, you will not be permitted to return to work unless the 
Company has or obtains evidence that it may, at its discretion, rely on in preference to the healthcare

grounds if it has any concerns about your health, irrespective of any received medical note or opinion.  
To manage sickness absence effectively and consistently we will seek to support staff during periods of 
illness and use the following interventions and procedures to facilitate a return to work, retain staff in 
employment and improve attendance. 
• Return to work discussions and interviews. 
• Keeping in touch during absence. 
• Monitoring and recording absence. 
• Carrying out sickness review meetings. 
• Providing management support. 
• Seeking medical reports and occupational health advice. 
 
Managing absence through these procedures or through the disciplinary process where appropriate.

Company may, following a return-to-work interview or during continuing absence, deal with it under the 
disciplinary procedure.  The disciplinary procedure will not, however, normally be used in cases of long-
term sickness absence, and a capability procedure may be invoked.  
Long term sickness  
While the Company is keen to assist employees who are absent, it cannot offer indefinite support. The 
Company will be eager to get any employees on long-term sickness absence back into the workplace as 
effectively as possible, but the employment may need to be terminated if this cannot be achieved. Once

The Company will usually require employees who have been absent for one month or more or are 
expected to be absent for one month or more, to return some or all their equipment. This may be 
requested so that the equipment can be redeployed to other employees. Equipment will be returned to

Reasonable adjustments 
The Company will comply with its obligations regarding the duty to make reasonable adjustments under 
the Equality Act 2010. Such adjustments may include a reduction in hours, the transfer of certain duties to 
other employees, physical adjustments, and retraining.  Such adjustments may be adopted on a

If you are off sick, we may want to refer you to Occupational Health to get more information about your 
condition. You do not have to agree, but if you do not, we will manage your absence based on the limited 
information we have received. 
Once your appointment is booked, it is important you attend. If you need to cancel or reschedule, you 
must contact HR immediately giving a minimum of 72 hours’ notice or a cancellation charge will be 
incurred.  Appointments are done by video conference, there is no requirement to travel.  
Disability-related absence 
If you think you have a disability, talk to your manager about it and discuss any adjustments you need.  
If you are off sick due to a disability-related illness, your manager will try to support you to return to work.

source_assertions.text:
Source assertion: Appendix J – Witness Statement of Arshad Shafi 
Background
1. My name is Arshad Shafi. I was employed by CACI Limited as a Senior Principal 
Consultant from October 2000. I am a British Pakistani Muslim man.
2. In 2001, I suffered a psychiatric breakdown following sustained racial and religious 
harassment while on assignment in Liverpool. Following this, I was placed on long-term 
sick leave, receiving two-thirds of my salary through the Respondent’s insurer, Unum.
3. In 2005, I attempted a phased return to work under medical supervision.
Events in 2005
4. At the start of my return, I had a meeting with Mr Jeet (Manjeet) Khaira, my Managing 
Director, and Miguel [surname if known]. In that meeting, I was informed that I would be 
assigned to Newcastle City Council in a Business Analyst role. I understood this to be a 
Principal Consultant-grade assignment. No mention was made of any demotion, and I was 
reassured and happy to be returning to proper work.

source_assertions.text:
Source assertion: Principal Consultant-grade assignment. No mention was made of any demotion, and I was 
reassured and happy to be returning to proper work.
5. On 1 July 2005, I had a further meeting with Mr Khaira in which he informed me that my 
grade and pay would be cut. In this meeting, I made a desperate plea for flexibility: as a 
single father, I asked to be allowed to start work at 10:00am instead of 9:30am every other 
Monday, to enable me to do the school run, and to work later until 6:00pm on those days.
6. This was a reasonable request, and I explained my situation clearly. However, Mr Khaira 
flatly rejected it, stating that CACI hours were 9:30 to 17:30 and that no adjustment would 
be made. I felt this was unnecessarily rigid and discriminatory, and designed to make my 
position untenable. It caused me significant distress.
7. On 1 July 2005, at the conclusion of my phased return, Mr Khaira informed me that I would

7. On 1 July 2005, at the conclusion of my phased return, Mr Khaira informed me that I would 
be demoted to a junior administrative role as a document writer, on a salary of only £24,000

8. The scale of this reduction was devastating. It caused a catastrophic relapse of my 
psychiatric condition. I realised that I would not be able to support my daughter, pay child 
support, or maintain my household.
Aftermath and Continuing Impact
9. I immediately lodged a grievance, but this was rejected by Mr Graham Post, the Finance 
Director. The grievance was not handled by HR, and no alternative review or welfare 
process was put in place. This reinforced my perception that CACI had no effective HR 
engagement with me following my relapse.

12.For many years, I also felt unable to pursue matters directly with CACI because the senior

prospect of having to confront or litigate against the same individual who had previously

avoidance. This was particularly acute because I remained employed by CACI, was 
financially dependent on PHI arrangements, and had no independent access to HR systems 
or internal support. While that power imbalance remained, I did not feel psychologically 
able to challenge my treatment.

13.After I became aware that Mr Khaira had left CACI in or around 2024, I felt, for the first 
time, able to seek assistance in relation to my situation. In or around December 2025, as my 
financial and administrative position continued to deteriorate, I approached Unite Legal 
Services for advice. I did so because my disability substantially affects my ability to initiate 
and navigate complex legal processes without external support, particularly where matters 
are prolonged, adversarial, or administratively complex.
14.Unite advised me that my Equality Act claims were unlikely to succeed on the basis that I 
was not actively attending the workplace and that any duty on CACI to make reasonable 
adjustments would only arise if and when I returned to work. I relied on that advice and did 
not pursue proceedings at that stage, understanding it to mean that there was no lawful 
mechanism available to me to challenge my continuing exclusion.

15.I now understand that this advice was incorrect in law, as confirmed by the Tribunal’s ruling 
at the Preliminary Hearing that my Equality Act claims fall within jurisdiction as an act 
extending over a period. I refer to these matters not to advance any legal argument, but to 
explain factually why I did not commence proceedings earlier and to demonstrate that I 
acted in good faith, sought professional assistance, and did not deliberately delay or 
acquiesce in the treatment complained of. Once it became clear to me that my exclusion was
part of an ongoing situation capable of legal challenge, I took steps to pursue my claim 
without further delay.

Source assertion: Appendix J – Witness Statement of Arshad Shafi 
Background
1. My name is Arshad Shafi. I was employed by CACI Limited as a Senior Principal 
Consultant from October 2000. I am a British Pakistani Muslim man.
2. In 2001, I suffered a psychiatric breakdown following sustained racial and religious 
harassment while on assignment in Liverpool. Following this, I was placed on long-term 
sick leave, receiving two-thirds of my salary through the Respondent’s insurer, Unum.
3. In 2005, I attempted a phased return to work under medical supervision.
Events in 2005
4. At the start of my return, I had a meeting with Mr Jeet (Manjeet) Khaira, my Managing 
Director, and Miguel [surname if known]. In that meeting, I was informed that I would be 
assigned to Newcastle City Council in a Business Analyst role. I understood this to be a 
Principal Consultant-grade assignment. No mention was made of any demotion, and I was 
reassured and happy to be returning to proper work.

This procedure should be read alongside the Company's Sickness Absence Policy and applies

1. My name is Arshad Shafi. I was employed by CACI Limited as a Senior Principal 
Consultant from October 2000. I am a British Pakistani Muslim man.
2. In 2001, I suffered a psychiatric breakdown following sustained racial and religious 
harassment while on assignment in Liverpool. Following this, I was placed on long-term 
sick leave, receiving two-thirds of my salary through the Respondent’s insurer, Unum.
3. In 2005, I attempted a phased return to work under medical supervision.
Events in 2005
4. At the start of my return, I had a meeting with Mr Jeet (Manjeet) Khaira, my Managing 
Director, and Miguel [surname if known]. In that meeting, I was informed that I would be 
assigned to Newcastle City Council in a Business Analyst role. I understood this to be a 
Principal Consultant-grade assignment. No mention was made of any demotion, and I was 
reassured and happy to be returning to proper work.

Bundle Section: Part 10 – Appendices

Summary
This appendix records the continuity of corporate leadership within CACI Limited relevant to the 
Claimant’s employment and subsequent dispute.

approximately 26 years’ service) and Mr Jeet Khaira (former Managing Director, Information & 
Management Systems Division, departed 2024) both held senior executive roles during and after the
period 2000 – 2005 that forms the basis of the Claimant’s case.
Their overlapping tenures demonstrate that CACI Ltd retains long-standing institutional knowledge 
of the events underlying this claim and continued access to relevant HR, occupational-health and 
insurer (Unum) records.

You asked whether I consider myself fit to return to work.

opinion regarding my current capability for work until an up-to-date Occupational Health 
assessment has been completed, relevant medical evidence has been obtained and any

upon my current medical condition and functional capacity, rather than solely upon 
historical medical evidence, and should take into account any reasonable adjustments that 
may enable me to return to work safely and sustainably.

Purpose and Principles 
This procedure should be read alongside the Company's Sickness Absence Policy and applies 
where an employee is unable to fulfil the requirements of their role due to ill health and dismissal 
on the grounds of capability is being considered. 
The Company will consider all relevant medical evidence, including Occupational Health advice, 
and whether any reasonable adjustments or suitable alternative employment would enable the 
employee to return to work. 
Where, following consultation and a review of the available evidence, the Company concludes 
that the employee is unable to perform the essential requirements of their role, with or without 
reasonable adjustments, and no suitable alternative employment is available, employment may 
be terminated on the grounds of capability, following the required statutory process. 
Where an employee who has been issued with notice of termination subsequently states that they

citations: Procedure_Managing Incapacity related to Capability.pdf, p.2
source_assertions.text:
Source assertion: be terminated on the grounds of capability, following the required statutory process. 
Where an employee who has been issued with notice of termination subsequently states that they 
are fit to return to work, the Company will not be required to withdraw that notice solely based 
on that assertion or evidence of an improvement in their condition. Any decision to withdraw 
notice will be based on a full assessment of the employee's ability to undertake the essential 
duties of their role on a sustained basis, considering up-to-date medical evidence, Occupational 
Health advice, the effectiveness of  any proposed adjustments, business requirements and the 
availability of a suitable role. 
Where the evidence does not support a sustainable return to work, or no reasonable adjustments 
would enable the employee to fulfil the requirements of the role, the dismissal on the grounds of 
capability may proceed.

If an employee is unwell during a period of annual leave, they should inform their manager of this on the 
first day of their sickness and provide a fit note which covers the full period of their absence. They will be 
considered unwell from the date outlined on the fit note. Where this process has been followed, they will 
be entitled to take the annual leave that fell within their period of ill health later.  
Return to work  
Where you wish to return to work prior to the date noted on a medical certificate / fit note you must 
obtain a signing off note from a healthcare professional prior to attending work.  Where your healthcare 
professional advises that you are not fit to return, you will not be permitted to return to work unless the 
Company has or obtains evidence that it may, at its discretion, rely on in preference to the healthcare

practitioner’s opinion. In any event, the Company reserves the right to suspend you on full p ay on medical 
grounds if it has any concerns about your health, irrespective of any received medical note or opinion.  
To manage sickness absence effectively and consistently we will seek to support staff during periods of 
illness and use the following interventions and procedures to facilitate a return to work, retain staff in 
employment and improve attendance. 
• Return to work discussions and interviews. 
• Keeping in touch during absence. 
• Monitoring and recording absence. 
• Carrying out sickness review meetings. 
• Providing management support. 
• Seeking medical reports and occupational health advice. 
 
Managing absence through these procedures or through the disciplinary process where appropriate.

Background

Consultant from October 2000. I am a British Pakistani Muslim man.
2. In 2001, I suffered a psychiatric breakdown following sustained racial and religious 
harassment while on assignment in Liverpool. Following this, I was placed on long-term 
sick leave, receiving two-thirds of my salary through the Respondent’s insurer, Unum.
3. In 2005, I attempted a phased return to work under medical supervision.
Events in 2005
4. At the start of my return, I had a meeting with Mr Jeet (Manjeet) Khaira, my Managing 
Director, and Miguel [surname if known]. In that meeting, I was informed that I would be 
assigned to Newcastle City Council in a Business Analyst role. I understood this to be a 
Principal Consultant-grade assignment. No mention was made of any demotion, and I was 
reassured and happy to be returning to proper work.

Sick notes scrapped by GPs in NHS trial to keep more UK workers in jobs
A major shake-up of Britain’s long-standing sick note system is about to begin, with GPs in someparts of England set to stop issuing ﬁt notes altogether as the Government launches acontroversial new trial focused on keeping more people in work.
The move comes amid growing concern over rising economic inactivity, mounting NHS pressureand the long-term impact of workers being signed oﬀ without wider support. More than 11million ﬁt notes were issued last year across the UK, with an overwhelming 93 per cent declaringworkers “not ﬁt for work”.
Now ministers believe the current approach may be pushing too many people away fromemployment instead of helping them recover safely while remaining connected to the workplace.

in establishing the adjustments that might be required. 
Occupational health  
If you are off sick, we may want to refer you to Occupational Health to get more information about your 
condition. You do not have to agree, but if you do not, we will manage your absence based on the limited 
information we have received. 
Once your appointment is booked, it is important you attend. If you need to cancel or reschedule, you 
must contact HR immediately giving a minimum of 72 hours’ notice or a cancellation charge will be 
incurred.  Appointments are done by video conference, there is no requirement to travel.  
Disability-related absence 
If you think you have a disability, talk to your manager about it and discuss any adjustments you need.  
If you are off sick due to a disability-related illness, your manager will try to support you to return to work.

Source assertion: Appendix J – Witness Statement of Arshad Shafi 
Background
1. My name is Arshad Shafi. I was employed by CACI Limited as a Senior Principal 
Consultant from October 2000. I am a British Pakistani Muslim man.
2. In 2001, I suffered a psychiatric breakdown following sustained racial and religious 
harassment while on assignment in Liverpool. Following this, I was placed on long-term 
sick leave, receiving two-thirds of my salary through the Respondent’s insurer, Unum.
3. In 2005, I attempted a phased return to work under medical supervision.
Events in 2005
4. At the start of my return, I had a meeting with Mr Jeet (Manjeet) Khaira, my Managing 
Director, and Miguel [surname if known]. In that meeting, I was informed that I would be 
assigned to Newcastle City Council in a Business Analyst role. I understood this to be a 
Principal Consultant-grade assignment. No mention was made of any demotion, and I was 
reassured and happy to be returning to proper work.

Source assertion: C&W WorkWell Referral Form
WorkWell is a programme funded by DWP and part of the UK Government’s measures to better
join up health and employment support . It aims to align the work and health landscape at local
level to support retention or return to employment for individuals with mental health or health-
related barriers. WorkWell can support an individual by providing:
Low intensity support for individuals either in work and struggling to retain or return to
their employment due to their mental health or a health-related work barrier
                                                                         or
Low intensity support for individuals recently unemployed and facing a barrier to return to
work due to mental health or a health-related work barrier.
WorkWell will provide support from a Journey Guide to explore support options and create a
tailored plan to retain or return to work.

source_assertions.text:
Source assertion: / © 2026 CACI Confidential     2 
Purpose and Principles 
This procedure should be read alongside the Company's Sickness Absence Policy and applies 
where an employee is unable to fulfil the requirements of their role due to ill health and dismissal 
on the grounds of capability is being considered. 
The Company will consider all relevant medical evidence, including Occupational Health advice, 
and whether any reasonable adjustments or suitable alternative employment would enable the 
employee to return to work. 
Where, following consultation and a review of the available evidence, the Company concludes 
that the employee is unable to perform the essential requirements of their role, with or without 
reasonable adjustments, and no suitable alternative employment is available, employment may 
be terminated on the grounds of capability, following the required statutory process. 
Where an employee who has been issued with notice of termination subsequently states that they

citations: Procedure_Managing Incapacity related to Capability.pdf, p.2
source_assertions.text:
Source assertion: be terminated on the grounds of capability, following the required statutory process. 
Where an employee who has been issued with notice of termination subsequently states that they 
are fit to return to work, the Company will not be required to withdraw that notice solely based 
on that assertion or evidence of an improvement in their condition. Any decision to withdraw 
notice will be based on a full assessment of the employee's ability to undertake the essential 
duties of their role on a sustained basis, considering up-to-date medical evidence, Occupational 
Health advice, the effectiveness of  any proposed adjustments, business requirements and the 
availability of a suitable role. 
Where the evidence does not support a sustainable return to work, or no reasonable adjustments 
would enable the employee to fulfil the requirements of the role, the dismissal on the grounds of 
capability may proceed.

Right of Appeal 
An employee who is dismissed on the grounds of capability may appeal the decision in writing 
within five working days of receiving the outcome letter, stating the grounds of appeal. An appeal 
meeting will be arranged and heard by a manager not previously i nvolved in the case where 
possible. The outcome of the appeal will be final. 
 
Special Considerations 
Pregnancy-related sickness absence, maternity leave, paternity leave, adoption leave, parental 
leave and time off for antenatal appointments will be managed in line with relevant legislation 
and Company policies and will not be considered when assessing attendance or capability under 
this procedure. 
 
The Company reserves the right to change this document at any time to reflect statutory 
changes or changes in Company Policy or process.

He argued that too many workers are being removed from the workplace prematurely whenﬂexible arrangements or adjusted duties may have allowed them to continue safely.

If workplace ﬂexibility becomes genuine and meaningful, many workers recovering from illnessor injury could beneﬁt from phased returns, amended duties or hybrid arrangements. General principles 
The Company aims to encourage all its employees to maximise their attendance at work whilst recognising 
that employees will, from time to time, be unable to come to work due to sickness.  
Whilst the Company understands that there will inevitably be some absence amongst employees, it must 
also pay due regard to its business needs. If an employee is frequently and persistently absent from work, 
this can damage efficiency and productivity, and  place an additional burden of work on the employee's 
colleagues.  
We will provide a healthy employment environment which promotes the wellbeing of all employees and 
reduces levels of absence, thereby ensuring effective service planning and delivery. We recognise the hard 
work of our employees and will assist those who have been absent to return to work as quickly and fully as

obtain a signing off note from a healthcare professional prior to attending work.  Where your healthcare

• Return to work discussions and interviews.

source_assertions.text:
Source assertion: Changes in Medical Circumstances 
When I completed the Claims Services International Declaration of Long-Term Incapacity 
in November 2025, my responses accurately reflected my circumstances at that time and 
were provided solely to assess entitlement under the Group Income Protection Scheme. 
Since then, my health has improved. In addition to ongoing treatment for my long-term 
mental health condition, I have been prescribed Wegovy (semaglutide) under medical 
supervision as part of a structured weight management programme. Together with lifestyle 
changes, this has enabled me to lose substantial weight, improve physical fitness, and 
enhance my overall wellbeing, which has positively impacted my mental health. 
While I continue to experience longstanding symptoms associated with Borderline 
Personality Disorder, anxiety, and depression—and am not suggesting I am currently fully 
fit to return—my health has improved noticeably since November 2025.

Despite the significant improvements in my physical health, I continue to experience symptoms associated with my
long-standing mental health condition. These symptoms fluctuate in severity but remain sufficiently significant to
affect my ability to function in demanding workplace environments.
My principal difficulties include:
Anxiety
I continue to experience anxiety, particularly when exposed to situations involving:
unfamiliar environments;
multiple competing demands;
excessive workplace pressure;
uncertainty; and
prolonged social interaction.
Stress Tolerance
I remain much less able than average to tolerate sustained psychological stress. When stress levels become

resilience.

Busy Working Environments
Busy offices, frequent interruptions, excessive background noise and constantly changing priorities are particularly
difficult for me. I function considerably better in environments that are:
quiet;
structured;
predictable; and
allow uninterrupted periods of concentration.
Travelling and Commuting
One of my most significant remaining difficulties relates to prolonged travelling. Lengthy commuting creates:
increased anxiety;
fatigue;
reduced concentration;
increased stress levels.
For this reason, I believe that home working or predominantly home-based hybrid working would significantly
reduce the impact of my condition.
Fatigue
Although my physical stamina has improved considerably, prolonged periods of psychological pressure continue to
produce mental fatigue. This differs from physical tiredness. Once mentally fatigued, I find it increasingly difficult to
maintain concentration and to process large amounts of information effectively.

Source assertion: Appendix J – Witness Statement of Arshad Shafi 
Background
1. My name is Arshad Shafi. I was employed by CACI Limited as a Senior Principal 
Consultant from October 2000. I am a British Pakistani Muslim man.
2. In 2001, I suffered a psychiatric breakdown following sustained racial and religious 
harassment while on assignment in Liverpool. Following this, I was placed on long-term 
sick leave, receiving two-thirds of my salary through the Respondent’s insurer, Unum.
3. In 2005, I attempted a phased return to work under medical supervision.
Events in 2005
4. At the start of my return, I had a meeting with Mr Jeet (Manjeet) Khaira, my Managing 
Director, and Miguel [surname if known]. In that meeting, I was informed that I would be 
assigned to Newcastle City Council in a Business Analyst role. I understood this to be a 
Principal Consultant-grade assignment. No mention was made of any demotion, and I was 
reassured and happy to be returning to proper work.

grade and pay would be cut. In this meeting, I made a desperate plea for flexibility: as a 
single father, I asked to be allowed to start work at 10:00am instead of 9:30am every other 
Monday, to enable me to do the school run, and to work later until 6:00pm on those days.
6. This was a reasonable request, and I explained my situation clearly. However, Mr Khaira 
flatly rejected it, stating that CACI hours were 9:30 to 17:30 and that no adjustment would 
be made. I felt this was unnecessarily rigid and discriminatory, and designed to make my 
position untenable. It caused me significant distress.
7. On 1 July 2005, at the conclusion of my phased return, Mr Khaira informed me that I would

Busy Working Environments
Busy offices, frequent interruptions, excessive background noise and constantly changing priorities are particularly
difficult for me. I function considerably better in environments that are:
quiet;
structured;
predictable; and
allow uninterrupted periods of concentration.
Travelling and Commuting
One of my most significant remaining difficulties relates to prolonged travelling. Lengthy commuting creates:
increased anxiety;
fatigue;
reduced concentration;
increased stress levels.
For this reason, I believe that home working or predominantly home-based hybrid working would significantly
reduce the impact of my condition.
Fatigue
Although my physical stamina has improved considerably, prolonged periods of psychological pressure continue to
produce mental fatigue. This differs from physical tiredness. Once mentally fatigued, I find it increasingly difficult to
maintain concentration and to process large amounts of information effectively.

Protection payments.

is a direct consequence of Respondent’s unlawful 
conduct in 2001–2005.

Background
1. My name is Arshad Shafi. I was employed by CACI Limited as a Senior Principal 
Consultant from October 2000. I am a British Pakistani Muslim man.
2. In 2001, I suffered a psychiatric breakdown following sustained racial and religious 
harassment while on assignment in Liverpool. Following this, I was placed on long-term

3. In 2005, I attempted a phased return to work under medical supervision.

Director, and Miguel [surname if known]. In that meeting, I was informed that I would be 
assigned to Newcastle City Council in a Business Analyst role. I understood this to be a 
Principal Consultant-grade assignment. No mention was made of any demotion, and I was 
reassured and happy to be returning to proper work.

Purpose and Principles 
This procedure should be read alongside the Company's Sickness Absence Policy and applies 
where an employee is unable to fulfil the requirements of their role due to ill health and dismissal 
on the grounds of capability is being considered. 
The Company will consider all relevant medical evidence, including Occupational Health advice, 
and whether any reasonable adjustments or suitable alternative employment would enable the 
employee to return to work. 
Where, following consultation and a review of the available evidence, the Company concludes 
that the employee is unable to perform the essential requirements of their role, with or without 
reasonable adjustments, and no suitable alternative employment is available, employment may 
be terminated on the grounds of capability, following the required statutory process. 
Where an employee who has been issued with notice of termination subsequently states that they

Where an employee who has been issued with notice of termination subsequently states that they 
are fit to return to work, the Company will not be required to withdraw that notice solely based 
on that assertion or evidence of an improvement in their condition. Any decision to withdraw 
notice will be based on a full assessment of the employee's ability to undertake the essential 
duties of their role on a sustained basis, considering up-to-date medical evidence, Occupational 
Health advice, the effectiveness of  any proposed adjustments, business requirements and the 
availability of a suitable role. 
Where the evidence does not support a sustainable return to work, or no reasonable adjustments 
would enable the employee to fulfil the requirements of the role, the dismissal on the grounds of 
capability may proceed.

Sick notes scrapped by GPs in NHS trial to keep more UK workers in jobs
A major shake-up of Britain’s long-standing sick note system is about to begin, with GPs in someparts of England set to stop issuing ﬁt notes altogether as the Government launches acontroversial new trial focused on keeping more people in work.
The move comes amid growing concern over rising economic inactivity, mounting NHS pressureand the long-term impact of workers being signed oﬀ without wider support. More than 11million ﬁt notes were issued last year across the UK, with an overwhelming 93 per cent declaringworkers “not ﬁt for work”.
Now ministers believe the current approach may be pushing too many people away fromemployment instead of helping them recover safely while remaining connected to the workplace.

If workplace ﬂexibility becomes genuine and meaningful, many workers recovering from illnessor injury could beneﬁt from phased returns, amended duties or hybrid arrangements. source_assertions.text:
Source assertion: manager will talk to you about the reason for your absence and about any concerns you may have, and about 
the impact of your absence and any next steps that might be taken. It is important to tell your manager if you 
think there may be underlying reasons for your absence, or if you were absent for a work-related reason. The 
return to work questions are listed below the self cert sickness form in CHRIS so just run through these and if 
there are no follow up actions then just state this. 
The purpose of such reviews will be to ensure that you are receiving appropriate support and to ensure that we 
have an up-to-date understanding of the latest medical situation and prognosis.  The specific issues that will be 
considered will be the likelihood of an improvement in your health and subsequent attendance, the availability 
of alternative work, the effect of past and future absences on the Company and whether there are any

citations: Sickness Absence Policy.pdf, p.6
source_assertions.text:
Source assertion: of alternative work, the effect of past and future absences on the Company and whether there are any 
reasonable adjustments which could be made regarding your work.  The review will also assist your Line 
Manager with forward planning.   
They will usually be conducted by your Line Manager and may involve the Director where appropriate.  You 
may be accompanied at any review by a trade union representative or work colleague. 
Absence monitoring / absence score 
The Company calculates absence scores using an industry standard formula called the Bradford Factor, to 
calculate the impact of employees’ sickness absences.  It works by looking at the total number of days 
absent multiplied by the number of episodes in the preceding 12 months squared. Monthly reports are 
provided to the relevant BU Head for their business unit.   
As examples: 
• If an employee is absent once in 52 weeks for 10 days, their absence score is: (1×1) x 10 = 10

citations: Sickness Absence Policy.pdf, p.8
source_assertions.text:
Source assertion: Company has or obtains evidence that it may, at its discretion, rely on in preference to the healthcare 
practitioner’s opinion. In any event, the Company reserves the right to suspend you on full p ay on medical 
grounds if it has any concerns about your health, irrespective of any received medical note or opinion.  
To manage sickness absence effectively and consistently we will seek to support staff during periods of 
illness and use the following interventions and procedures to facilitate a return to work, retain staff in 
employment and improve attendance. 
• Return to work discussions and interviews. 
• Keeping in touch during absence. 
• Monitoring and recording absence. 
• Carrying out sickness review meetings. 
• Providing management support. 
• Seeking medical reports and occupational health advice. 
 
Managing absence through these procedures or through the disciplinary process where appropriate.

citations: Sickness Absence Policy.pdf, p.8

the employee has exhausted their 28-week entitlement to statutory sick pay, or before, the employee’s

The Company will usually require employees who have been absent for one month or more or are 
expected to be absent for one month or more, to return some or all their equipment. This may be 
requested so that the equipment can be redeployed to other employees. Equipment will be returned to

citations: Sickness Absence Policy.pdf, p.9
source_assertions.text:
Source assertion: If you are off sick due to a disability-related illness, your manager will try to support you to return to work. 
They might refer you to Occupational Health to find out more about your condition, how it may affect you 
at work and whether there are any adjustments we could make to help. 
These absences might count towards the absence triggers in some circumstances. However, it might be a 
reasonable adjustment to agree a revised absence trigger with you for absences related to a disability or 
to not include them when calculating absences triggers. If you have any questions or concerns about 
disability-related absence, speak to your manager. Managers should contact HR for advice on revising 
absence triggers for employees with disabilities. 
Alternative employment 
If you are unable to return to your own job, your Line Manager and HR will consider suitable alternative 
employment, although we will not be obliged to create new positions for this purpose.

citations: Sickness Absence Policy.pdf, p.10
source_assertions.text:
Source assertion: possible. There are additional considerations where the health condition may be classed as a disability 
under the Equality Act 2010, guidance should be sought from HR.  
Staff who require planned medical procedures, will be entitled to sick leave for the procedure and 
recovery time. 
Reasonable requests for time off to accompany a close family member (parent/child/partner) to medical 
appointments must be agreed with your manager. You will be asked to book annual leave, alternatively 
this can be granted as unpaid leave. In more severe circumstances, compassionate leave may be 
appropriate. 
Lateness 
Lateness (i.e., failure to attend work at agreed times), where associated with short term frequent 
absences, will be included within an employee’s attendance record, and managed within the attendance 
review procedure and, where appropriate, our disciplinary procedure. 
Lateness which is not associated with short term frequent absences will be investigated and managed

citations: Sickness Absence Policy.pdf, p.10
source_assertions.text:
Source assertion: review procedure and, where appropriate, our disciplinary procedure. 
Lateness which is not associated with short term frequent absences will be investigated and managed 
through our disciplinary or capability procedure as appropriate. 
Unauthorised absence 
Unauthorised absence, for example leaving the Company’s premises without permission or failing to 
comply with our notification and certification procedures are usually regarded as disciplinary matters and 
will be dealt with under our disciplinary procedure. 
Further support 
If you have any questions about how you need to report your absence or about the Company’s approach 
to managing absence, please speak to your manager. If managers need advice, they should contact HR.  
We have an Employee Assistance Programme (EAP) who can provide employees with support. You can 
contact the EAP on 0800 023 2269.

evidence_keys: 8081166d-9889-40bb-8add-5d0893037ff0__Appendix H5 – Return to Work (RTW) Correspondence – May 2005_2_1
source_assertions.text:
Source assertion: Relevance to the Claim
1. Confirms that CACI were planning the Claimant’s return to work, and that Jeet Khaira 
and Nigel Phillips had direct managerial involvement.
2. The statement “if all goes well” by HR on behalf of Jeet Khaira shows the anticipated 
outcome of the meeting – a critical precursor to the subsequent demotion and pay cut.
3. Demonstrates CACI’s awareness of the need for reasonable adjustments and structured 
rehabilitation, as advised by UnumProvident, yet these steps were never implemented.
4. Corroborates that the Claimant was fit, willing and proactive in returning to work, refuting 
any assertion that he was disengaged or unfit.
5. Supports claims under:
• s.15 Equality Act 2010 – Discrimination arising from disability (adverse treatment 
following disability-related absence);
• s.20 EqA 2010 – Failure to make reasonable adjustments; and
• s.98 Employment Rights Act 1996 – Unfair dismissal (procedural and substantive).

source_assertions.text:

Relevance to the Claim
1. Establishes a formally approved RTW plan, demonstrating CACI’s full awareness of 
medical and insurer recommendations.
2. Confirms CACI’s knowledge of the duty to make reasonable adjustments, yet the plan 
was not followed or maintained, leading directly to the Claimant’s demotion.
3. Proves that the Claimant was fit, willing, and medically cleared to return under 
supervision.
4. Demonstrates that Jeet Khaira, Christine McCarroll, Nigel Phillips, and Terry 
Williamson were all actively involved — proving senior-level decision-making.
5. The seven-week plan evidences that any sudden demotion shortly afterward was contrary to
agreed rehabilitation protocols, amounting to unfavourable treatment arising from 
disability (s.15 EqA 2010) and a failure to make reasonable adjustments (s.20 EqA 
2010).
